title: Introduce websocket-backed dynamic tool-binding agent quickstart and TypeScript devcontainer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add websocket-based agent quickstart demonstrating dynamic tool binding and a TypeScript devcontainer for fast onboarding. Includes README, example tools, tests and CI smoke checks.
description: Motivation: provide a compact, reproducible quickstart that demonstrates dynamic runtime tool binding over a websocket transport for agent/tool-calling flows. Many teams build agents that need to attach/detach tools at runtime (credit-card style connectors, ephemeral DB read-only adapters, external webhook proxies). This quickstart shows how to: 1) expose a tiny tools registry over a websocket channel, 2) let the agent discover and bind tools on the fly, and 3) run the whole example inside a TypeScript devcontainer for consistent local dev and CI. This PR contains: - a new example app under examples/ws-agent/ that simulates three tool types (search, calculator, and http-fetch) and a minimal registry service that announces available tools via websocket messages; - a TypeScript Devcontainer configured to run the example in a reproducible environment (.devcontainer/); - an expanded README with step-by-step local run instructions, debugging tips, and API contract examples; - unit + integration smoke tests and a lightweight e2e harness that exercises dynamic tool attach/detach scenarios. Checklist: - [x] implement websocket registry and stub tools - [x] agent wiring + typed tool bindings in TypeScript - [x] add devcontainer + Dockerfile for consistent env - [x] tests (unit + smoke e2e) - [x] README and quickstart commands - [x] CI job added to examples pipeline How to run locally (short): 1) git checkout feature/ws-dynamic-tool-binding-quickstart 2) cd examples/ws-agent && yarn && yarn dev:registry 3) in another shell yarn dev:agent --connect ws://localhost:8080 4) open the simple playground at http://localhost:3000 to step through bind/unbind sequences Notes on design decisions: - websocket transport was chosen to keep the demo lightweight and to model long-lived tool metadata syncs (vs polling). The agent subscribes to registry messages and performs optimistic binds; a small lease/heartbeat keeps the example resilient. - dynamic binding surface is intentionally minimal: tools expose a short JSON schema and an invocation path; the agent uses a small adapter layer to coerce results into a structured function-call style response compatible with Redwood's tool-calling conventions. - Devcontainer pins node and yarn versions to avoid local drift and removes friction for new contributors. Compatibility: this example targets the Redwood JavaScript SDK v0.18+ (see README). It does not change existing platform surface or APIs. Files changed summary: - examples/ws-agent/README.md: long-form quickstart, API contract, troubleshooting, and observability tips - examples/ws-agent/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json and Dockerfile: reproducible dev env - examples/ws-agent/src/registry.ts: websocket registry simulator - examples/ws-agent/src/agent.ts: agent binding logic and adapter layer - examples/ws-agent/src/tools/*.ts: stub tool implementations (search, calc, http-fetch) - examples/ws-agent/test/e2e/smoke.spec.ts: e2e smoke harness - .github/workflows/examples-ci.yml: added examples/ws-agent smoke stage Commits (high level): - 0a1b6f4 add ws-agent scaffold, devcontainer, and initial README - 9d3f2b1 implement registry, tool stubs and agent binding adapter - b4e9c2a add smoke e2e tests and CI job; fix flaky timing in registry - f7a12d0 docs: expand quickstart and troubleshooting Review conversation (condensed): "Rina Kato: Nice! Can you clarify the security model for the registry messages? We shouldn't assume any auth in example code without a clear note." "Maya Chen: Added a thorough section in README noting this is a local/dev-only demo and included an optional AUTH_TOKEN env var to gate the registry; clarified lease semantics and recommended production alternatives (mTLS, IAM)." "Diego Alvarez: Tests look flaky locally due to timing of ws reconnects; suggest using deterministic timers in registry for CI." "Maya Chen: switched registry to a deterministic start sequence in tests and added a short retry policy in agent, reduced flakiness in CI." "Samir Bose: Approving after minor README edits (IMHO add an example of a tool schema with required/optional fields)." CI and flakes: initial CI run showed a transient timing test failure on the registry (race in ws startup). I pushed a fix (b4e9c2a) that adds an explicit readiness message from the registry and retries in the agent harness; CI re-run passed. QA and testing: added e2e smoke that runs in the examples CI matrix on a single linux node; tests exercise bind, invoke, and unbind lifecycle and assert telemetry/diagnostic events are emitted to stdout (sufficient for example verification). Documentation: README includes: - quickstart steps (devcontainer and local) - API contract: websocket messages (announce, bind, heartbeat, unannounce, invoke) with example payloads - debugging tips for common races and curl/sample json invocations - recommended production next steps (auth, validation, and telemetry) Reasons to merge: - increases the catalog of dynamic tool examples available to customers building agent architectures - provides a reproducible dev environment (devcontainer) to lower onboarding cost - includes tests and CI making the example maintainable and reliable Post-merge followups (tracked in ENG-1931): - wire a small Playground recipe demonstrating tool schema evolution and migration - add a Go / Python minimal client adapters recipe (community request)
